headline: US-Israel plan renewed Iran strikes AFTER US midterms (NYT Oct 21) + Trump 'something is going to happen very soon' + Netanyahu
dek: NYT: US and Israel have drawn up specific plans for a short, intensive post-midterm operation on Iran (energy sites, nuclear facilities, missile/drone arsenal; refineries reportedly spared to avoid gasoline prices); militaries stepped up exercises including over-Iraq flyovers; Hegseth met…
sources: NYT (anonymous US officials); Haaretz; Times of Israel; Business Times; Trump Truth Social/airfield remarks; Netanyahu Oct 22 denial; IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi via SNN (Iranian state-affiliated); IAF commander Maj G
fault_line: Do three-day bombing campaigns ever force concessions — or do they just buy the next war?

sections.what_happened: NYT: US and Israel have drawn up specific plans for a short, intensive post-midterm operation on Iran (energy sites, nuclear facilities, missile/drone arsenal; refineries reportedly spared to avoid gasoline prices); militaries stepped up exercises including over-Iraq flyovers; Hegseth met Netanyahu in Israel this week. Trump Wed night: US 'not negotiating with Iran' and 'something is going to happen very soon... Most people think it will happen after the elections.' Netanyahu Thursday: reports of the talks are 'incorrect,' would not elaborate. IRGC spokesman Mohebbi: 'The United States has the Mother of All Bombs. We will show them the Father of All Bombs.' IAF commander Tischler: an Air Force-wide Iran strike was halted one hour before take-off due to US pressure (Business Times independently notes Trump vetoed strike plans in October).
sections.what_verified: NYT report carried independently by Haaretz, ToI, ET, Republic, Business Times; Trump veto of October strike prep independently noted by Business Times; Hegseth-Netanyahu meeting consistent across outlets.
sections.what_disputed: All plan details rest on anonymous officials — Trump has repeatedly vetoed strike plans in 2026, including in October; Netanyahu denies the reporting; no official order or authorization confirmed.
sections.why_matters: The plan exists on paper, the finger is not on the button: who actually holds the kill-switch (Trump, who keeps vetoing) and why the clock runs to Nov 3 midterms. Present as attributed plan-reporting, never as imminent fact; Iran's voice (Rezaei, IRGC) gets its own screen.
sections.context: Background: US-Israel plan renewed Iran strikes AFTER US midterms (NYT Oct 21) + Trump 'something is going to happen very soon' + Netanyahu denial + IRGC 'father of all bombs' threat

totw_analysis: Our read: The plan exists on paper, the finger is not on the button: who actually holds the kill-switch (Trump, who keeps vetoing) and why the clock runs to Nov 3 midterms. Present as attributed plan-reporting, never as imminent fact; Iran's voice (Rezaei, IRGC) gets its own screen. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Do three-day bombing campaigns ever force concessions — or do they just buy the next war?
